doc.title: Marty Morell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Continuity of the Ellington band and why he resigned
summary: Positions pass down the band; he worked with last-link Barrie Lee Hall and Rocky White, and left after about six years because of travel.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: It’s interesting that the band has retained that – or retained that kind of feel with some of the key players having passed away or whatever. You don’t have Johnny Hodges there anymore but if they’re still laying back as you say.

Well the thing is that that band is actually from the original times when Duke started it, right, so it would go along and when somebody died, that position got filled, right? So they kept everything going. You know Duke passed and Mercer took over, and some of

the guys that had worked with Duke still stayed in the band so it was kind of always passing the flag to the next person. So there was a certain way to play in that band and that’s what — if you could do that then you got the gig, that type of thing. Right? So I’m honored to have been part of that Ellington legacy even though – actually I worked with Barry Lee Hall. Barry Lee Hall unfortunately passed away a few years ago. He was a trumpet player and he worked with Ellington. All right? So he was the last connection. And also Rocky White, the drummer, Duke Ellington himself hired Rocky, right? And he was with the band for 35, 38 years, something like that. So to get a position in that band somebody has to die. Then you get a position.
That’s right. There’s this – Ellington never fired anyone I guess, at least that’s what I’ve read.

Well I guess that’s true because if the cats accepted you or wanted you then you’re up to the task, you’re up to playing the right way. So I actually resigned about four or five years ago, because I thought I want to leave on my own terms. I’m not going to wait until I die.
I have other things I can do.

Well actually I just didn’t want to do the traveling anymore and I thought it was better for the band to get somebody that could do all the gigs. Actually last year I did a few gigs. They were here in Florida and the drummer couldn’t make it so I filled in.
Yeah, you get tired of the traveling.
